1.rendering: Rendered "podjęło trud spisania po kolei tego wszystkiego, co dokonało się pośród nas i wypełniło do końca" to carry both Luke's historiographic claim (orderly, sequential account) and the πεπληροφορημένων sense of events brought to fulfillment. "Wypełniło do końca" preserves the theological weight of completion that bare "happened among us" would flatten.
1.tradeOff: Slightly longer than a clipped "co się wypełniło"; chose the doubled phrasing because the perfect-passive force in Greek implies divine bringing-to-fullness, not mere occurrence.

3.rendering: Rendered κράτιστε Θεόφιλε as "dostojny Teofilu, którego hojności dzieło to wiele zawdzięcza" — the honorific "dostojny" carries the high-status κράτιστε, and the added clause makes the patronage transaction visible in the running text so a modern reader feels the social weight (this was a funded dedication, not a private letter).
3.tradeOff: Adds material not in the Greek; without it the patron-client dynamic disappears entirely for a modern reader who reads "Theophilus" as just a name. The must-land friction (honor/shame, patronage as social transaction) justified the amplification.

5.rendering: Expanded "za czasów Heroda, króla Judei" with "gdy nad krajem ciążyła jego podejrzliwa, brutalna władza" — sets the political atmosphere of fear that frames the whole infancy narrative, so the angelic "do not be afraid" lands against a real backdrop rather than a neutral date-stamp.
5.tradeOff: Heavier opening than the Greek's bare temporal marker; chose to let modern readers feel the menace that first-century hearers would have heard in "Herod" alone.

5.rendering: Added "jednej z dwudziestu czterech zmian, które po kolei pełniły służbę w świątyni" inline to explain ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά rather than footnote it. Without this, the lottery in v.9 has no context — readers cannot feel how rare Zechariah's selection was.
5.tradeOff: Inline explanation lengthens v.5; chose this over a footnote because it sets up the once-in-a-lifetime weight of v.9.

9.rendering: Closed v.9 with "Taki zaszczyt spotykał kapłana raz w życiu, jeśli w ogóle" — landing the must-land friction that being chosen by lot for the incense offering was the apex of a priest's career, often never reached. The "jeśli w ogóle" carries the bitterness that for many priests it never came.
9.tradeOff: Explicit gloss inside the verse rather than a footnote; the offense (this was THE moment of Zechariah's life) must be felt, and modern readers have no cultural frame for temple lotteries.

13.rendering: Kept "Twoja modlitwa została wysłuchana" — neutral perfect-passive that does not specify which prayer (for a son, or for Israel's redemption). Polish εἰσηκούσθη maps cleanly here without amplification.
13.tradeOff: None — the ambiguity is in the Greek and should remain in the Polish.

15.rendering: Rendered "Nie będzie pił wina ani niczego mocnego" without explicit Nazirite labeling. The dietary prohibition signals the consecration; Polish "niczego mocnego" covers σίκερα (strong drink) without a loanword.
15.tradeOff: Readers who know the Nazirite vow will catch it; others will read consecration without the technical category. Acceptable since John's prophetic identity is carried by the Elijah comparison in v.17.

17.rendering: Rendered "przywrócić sposób myślenia ludzi prawych" for ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων — "sposób myślenia" carries φρόνησις (practical wisdom/disposition) better than the wooden "mądrość"; "ludzi prawych" carries δικαίων as a human category rather than abstract justice.
17.tradeOff: Longer than a clipped "do mądrości sprawiedliwych"; chose precision over compression because the Malachi 4 allusion's force is in changed disposition, not just "wisdom."

20.rendering: "Oniemiejesz i nie będziesz mógł wymówić ani słowa" — doubled phrasing carries the κωφός + μὴ δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι intensification (mute AND unable to speak), preserving the sign-as-discipline weight that a single "zaniemówisz" would soften.
20.tradeOff: Slight redundancy; chose it because the punishment-for-doubt is the must-land tension that resolves only in v.64.

25.rendering: "Zdjął ze mnie hańbę, którą musiałam znosić w oczach ludzi" — "musiałam znosić" carries the long endurance, and "w oczach ludzi" locates the shame socially (where it belongs) rather than theologically. Honors the harm-history note: barrenness is never moral failure in the text.
25.tradeOff: "Musiałam znosić" adds duration not strictly in the Greek; chose it so the reader feels Elizabeth's years of stigma, not a momentary embarrassment.

26.rendering: "Nazaretu, małej wioski w Galilei, o której świat nigdy nie słyszał" — landing the class/reversal friction inline. Without the gloss, Nazareth reads to modern Polish readers as a known biblical place; the original force (nowhere village) is lost.
26.tradeOff: Explicit editorial framing; chose it because the reversal theme (peasant girl from nowhere receives royal promise) starts here and must be felt, not footnoted.

27.rendering: Expanded the bare "zaręczonej z mężczyzną" with the full inline explanation of betrothal-as-binding and the capital-offense danger of perceived adultery. The original audience knew this; modern Polish readers do not, and the rest of the pericope (Mary's question in v.34, her courage in v.38) is unreadable without it.
27.tradeOff: Significant amplification — the longest single expansion in the chapter. Chose it because betrothal customs are the load-bearing context for Mary's risk; demoting this to a footnote guts the must-land friction (Mary's yes was socially dangerous, potentially fatal).

34.rendering: "Jak to się stanie? ... Gdybym teraz zaszła w ciążę, wzięto by mnie za cudzołożnicę." Amplified Mary's question to make explicit what the Greek implies through the betrothal context already set up in v.27 — her objection is not just biological but social/legal.
34.tradeOff: Adds content beyond the Greek's compact ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω. Justified because the must-land friction (capital danger) lands in Mary's own voice rather than as narrator commentary.

35.rendering: Added "jak obłok kiedyś okrył namiot spotkania" inline for ἐπισκιάσει — the LXX echo (Exod 40:35) is the whole theological weight of the verb. Polish "okryje" alone would read as physical covering; the inline gloss surfaces the Shekinah allusion.
35.tradeOff: Explicit OT cross-reference inside the running text; chose it because the verb's force is the temple-glory echo and Polish lacks a verb that carries it on its own.

38.rendering: "Należę do Pana" for ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη κυρίου — chose "należę" over the more literal "jestem służebnicą" to land the costly self-handing-over without the diminutive softness "służebnica" can carry in Polish. "Należę" carries belonging-under-authority.
38.tradeOff: Loses the explicit "servant" word that has liturgical resonance; chose force-of-commitment over title because the must-land point is Mary's faith-response, not a title.

42.rendering: "Wydała głośny okrzyk i zawołała na cały dom" for ἀνεφώνησεν κραυγῇ μεγάλῃ — doubled phrasing carries the prophetic, public force; "na cały dom" makes the publicness audible. The honor/shame inversion (elder priest's wife defers to peasant girl) needs the volume to land.
42.tradeOff: Slight redundancy of "głośny okrzyk" + "zawołała"; chose it because the prophetic outburst is the point — Elizabeth is not whispering.

43.rendering: "Czym ja na to zasłużyłam" for πόθεν μοι τοῦτο — the Polish idiom carries the "how did I deserve this" reversal-of-status more naturally than "skąd mi to." Lands the inversion: the older, higher-status woman acknowledging the younger as superior.
43.tradeOff: Slight shift from "whence" to "by what merit"; chose the idiomatic Polish because the social reversal is the must-land point and the literal "skąd" reads flat.

46.rendering: "Wszystko we mnie wielbi Pana" for μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν κύριον — "wszystko we mnie" carries the totality of ψυχή better than the wooden "moja dusza," and avoids the cold archaism that would distance modern Polish readers from Mary's voice. Echoes the personal-praise opening that Bock identifies (vv.46-50).
46.tradeOff: Loses the explicit "soul" word with its liturgical weight; chose immediacy over liturgical familiarity because this is a young woman speaking from her gut, not chanting Vespers.

48.rendering: "Na nikogo, na dziewczynę z samego dołu" for ἐπὶ τὴν ταπείνωσιν — "z samego dołu" lands the class/economic force (peasant from the bottom of the social ladder) that "uniżenie" or "pokorę" would moralize. The reversal theme requires economic specificity.
48.tradeOff: Sacrifices the spiritual-humility reading that "uniżenie" carries; chose social-class force because the Magnificat's center (vv.51-53) is explicitly economic/political reversal, not interior virtue.

51.rendering: "Pokazał, jak silne jest Jego ramię" — kept the Hebraism "ramię" with the visible-demonstration gloss, so the cosmic-reversal section (vv.51-53) opens with God's power made manifest, matching the rationale's note that the child in Mary's womb is the agent of the reversal — God's "arm" made visible.
51.tradeOff: Slight expansion of ἐποίησεν κράτος; chose it so the section's pivot from personal praise to cosmic action is unmissable.

52.rendering: "Władców zrzucił z tronów, a tych z samego dołu podniósł wysoko" — "władców" carries δυνάστας as political rulers (not abstract "the mighty"); "z samego dołu" echoes v.48's class language to bind Mary's experience to the universal pattern.
52.tradeOff: None — the political/economic reversal is must-land friction; softening it ("możnych," "pokornych") would moralize what the Greek leaves concrete and material.

53.rendering: "Głodnych nasycił dobrem, a bogatych odprawił z pustymi rękami" — kept the stark economic contrast. "Z pustymi rękami" carries κενούς with maximum bite; no softening to "odesłał ich" or similar.
53.tradeOff: None — the must-land friction is the concrete economic reversal; any abstraction ("those who are full," "those in need") guts it.

60.rendering: "Nie. Będzie się nazywał Jan" — the bare "Nie" at the start carries Elizabeth's authoritative break from custom. A woman overriding patriarchal naming was the shock; the curt "Nie" lands the surprise that v.61 then voices.
60.tradeOff: More abrupt than a smooth "Nie, będzie nazywał się Jan"; chose the staccato so readers feel the social rupture (women did not typically control naming).

63.rendering: "I wszyscy oniemieli, że ojciec przyznał rację matce" — added gloss for ἐθαύμασαν πάντες. The astonishment is not generic; it is specifically that the patriarch backed the mother's break with naming custom. Without the gloss, modern readers miss why everyone is amazed.
63.tradeOff: Editorial amplification of a single verb; chose it because the gender-and-authority friction is must-land — Elizabeth's insistence + Zechariah's agreement is the resolution of the muteness-as-discipline arc.

64.rendering: "W tej samej chwili otworzyły mu się usta, odzyskał mowę" — doubled the action (mouth opened + speech returned) to carry ἀνεῴχθη ... καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα αὐτοῦ. The two-verb structure matches the Greek's emphasis on the dual reversal of the v.20 silencing.
64.tradeOff: Slight redundancy; chose it because the symmetry with v.20's doubled muteness ("oniemiejesz i nie będziesz mógł wymówić ani słowa") is structurally important.

69.rendering: "Wzbudził dla nas potężnego Wybawcę" for κέρας σωτηρίας — replaced the dead metaphor ("róg zbawienia" reads as nonsense in Polish) with its meaning. The horn-image conveyed power/salvation to ancient hearers; modern Polish readers need the force, not the image.
69.tradeOff: Loses the OT horn-metaphor that connects to Davidic/messianic texts; chose comprehension because the metaphor is dead in Polish and would create friction in the wrong place (incomprehension rather than wonder).

71.rendering: "Ocali od wrogów, wyrwie z rąk wszystkich, którzy nas nienawidzą" — kept the doubled enemy-language without softening to spiritual abstraction. The must-land friction is that first-century Jews heard this against Roman occupation; the language must remain political/material.
71.tradeOff: Modern Polish readers may import contemporary political enemies; accepted that risk because the Benedictus's force is liberation-language, not interior-spiritual rescue.

78.rendering: "Z trzewi Bożego miłosierdzia, które wzbiera w Nim nad nami" for διὰ σπλάγχνα ἐλέους — kept "trzewi" (guts/bowels) for σπλάγχνα. Polish "trzewi" is the right word: visceral, embodied, not the sanitized "serce." "Wzbiera" carries the welling-up motion that the Greek's seat-of-compassion implies.
78.tradeOff: "Trzewi" may feel jarring or earthy to liturgical ears; chose it because σπλάγχνα is precisely an earthy, gut-level word, and softening it to "serce" or "miłosierdzie" alone loses the bodily force.

79.rendering: "Poprowadzić nasze kroki na drogę pokoju" — kept the gentle Isaianic close as the final word of the Benedictus, honoring the rationale's note that the path of peace is the final word, balancing the reversal language of vv.51-53.
79.tradeOff: None — the closing's tonal shift from liberation-language to peace is intentional and must remain.

80.rendering: "Rósł i nabierał siły ducha. Mieszkał na pustkowiu" — kept the bare summary; the unanswered tension ("what then will this child become?" from v.66) is meant to hang. No amplification, because the chapter's deliberate closure is to leave John offstage until chapter 3.
80.tradeOff: None — restraint is the point. Adding anticipatory color would prematurely close the gap Luke intentionally leaves open.
